rules: HM Land Registry's National Polygon Dataset is the published dataset of HMLR Index Polygons for England and Wales.
On completion of a registered title HMLR normally produces a title plan, a register and one or more index polygons.
The title plan and register record the general position of registered-title boundaries unless a boundary has been determined as exact.
An index polygon forms part of the statutory Index referenced by section 68 of the Land Registration Act 2002.
An index polygon also relates to rule 10 of the Land Registration Rules 2003.
The purpose of an index polygon is to provide an index showing the indicative location of a registered title.
HM Land Registry holds index polygons in vector format.
The title plan and register share the title number identifier.
Every registered title has at least one index polygon.
Each index polygon has a unique Poly_ID.
The relationship between a registered title and its index polygons is managed through the title number.
HM Land Registry index polygons are mapped against Ordnance Survey MasterMap large-scale data.
Index polygons follow MasterMap features where those mapped features relate to the ownership boundary.
Ownership boundaries do not always follow features mapped in MasterMap.
The National Polygon Dataset is a subset of the Land Register containing registered titles relating to land or property.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to the Title Descriptor dataset.
The National Polygon Dataset is closely linked to the Title Number and UPRN Look Up dataset.
The three National Polygon Service datasets are separated to make them smaller and easier to manage and maintain.
The title number provides the linking identifier between National Polygon and other HMLR datasets.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of the National Polygon Dataset.
INSPIRE Index Polygons carry a simpler attribute set including identifier, creation date and polygon last-updated date.
The National Polygon Shape field is mandatory geometry.
The National Polygon Shape geometry must be a single area.
The National Polygon Poly_ID field is a mandatory numeric field.
Poly_ID is unique to the spatial object and managed through dataset lifecycle rules.
The National Polygon Title_No field is a mandatory character field.
The National Polygon INSERT field is a mandatory date recording initial polygon creation on the index map.
The National Polygon UPDATE field is a mandatory date recording when all or part of the title was last updated.
The National Polygon Vers_No field is a mandatory numeric version of Poly_ID.
The National Polygon Rec_Status field is a mandatory character field.
National Polygon Rec_Status value A means Added.
National Polygon Rec_Status value C means Changed.
National Polygon Rec_Status value D means Deleted.
Where registrations are intended to adjoin, minor index-polygon discrepancies are expected to be resolved during registration practice.
Registered titles that are not intended to adjoin can legitimately leave gaps between index polygons.
An index polygon may be the same size as, larger than or smaller than the extent shown on the title plan.
Index polygons should not be relied on to show the exact extent of registered titles.
The National Polygon Dataset contains inconsistencies arising from former capture practices.
Historic index polygons were manually captured on Ordnance Survey county-series sheets.
Historic index polygons were also manually captured on national-grid sheets.
Historic index polygons were also maintained in parcels books.
In February 2004 HMLR completed conversion of about 19 million paper index polygons to vector polygons.
The 2004 vectorised polygons were mapped against Ordnance Survey Land-Line.
The National Polygon Dataset is published and then updated monthly.
National Polygon Service files are updated and available from the second working day of each month.
National Polygon subscribers receive the full dataset, change-only updates and validation files.
National Polygon CSV files use comma separators, ASCII character 44.
National Polygon CSV files enclose all fields in double quotes, ASCII character 34.
Blank National Polygon CSV fields are represented by empty quoted strings.
National Polygon CSV dates use DD-MM-YYYY format.
National Polygon CSV files use UTF-8 encoding.
National Polygon CSV delivery removes line separation within fields.
The first row of National Polygon CSV files contains column headings.
The National Polygon full extract is split into multiple files with a 2GB limit.
National Polygon full files follow the LR_POLY_FULL_<month>_<file number> naming pattern.
National Polygon change-only files follow the LR_POLY_COU_<DD_MMM_YYYY> naming pattern.
National Polygon validation files follow the LR_POLY_VALI_<month> naming pattern.
The National Polygon Service reports more than 25 million titles.
The National Polygon Service reports about 28 million polygons.
The National Polygon Service contains National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number/UPRN Look Up datasets.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
A coordinate entity query constructs a point from latitude and longitude and returns intersecting geometries.
The longitude parameter requires latitude to be supplied.
The latitude parameter requires longitude to be supplied.
The q parameter can search by postcode.
The q parameter can search by Unique Property Reference Number.
The typology parameter filters entities by typology.
The dataset parameter filters entities by dataset.
The organisation_entity parameter filters entities managed by an organisation.
The entity parameter filters by entity number.
The curie parameter filters by CURIE.
The prefix parameter filters by prefix.
The reference parameter filters by reference.
The period parameter can select current or all entries.
The start_date_year parameter filters by start-date year.
The start_date_month parameter filters by start-date month.
The start_date_day parameter filters by start-date day.
start_date_match accepts match.
start_date_match accepts before.
start_date_match accepts since.
start_date_match can be left empty.
The end_date_year parameter filters by end-date year.
The end_date_month parameter filters by end-date month.
The end_date_day parameter filters by end-date day.
end_date_match accepts match.
end_date_match accepts before.
end_date_match accepts since.
end_date_match can be left empty.
The entry_date_year parameter filters by entry-date year.
The entry_date_month parameter filters by entry-date month.
The entry_date_day parameter filters by entry-date day.
entry_date_match accepts match.
entry_date_match accepts before.
entry_date_match accepts since.
entry_date_match can be left empty.
The geometry parameter accepts one or more WKT geometries.
The geometry_entity parameter uses geometries from supplied entity IDs.
The geometry_reference parameter uses geometries from entities matching supplied references.
The geometry_curie parameter uses geometries from entities matching supplied CURIEs.
geometry_relation accepts within.
geometry_relation accepts equals.
geometry_relation accepts disjoint.
geometry_relation accepts intersects.
geometry_relation accepts touches.
geometry_relation accepts contains.
geometry_relation accepts covers.
geometry_relation accepts coveredby.
geometry_relation accepts overlaps.
geometry_relation accepts crosses.
The limit parameter sets the maximum number of entity results.
The offset parameter paginates entity results.
The field parameter selects fields to include in a response.
The exclude_field parameter selects fields to exclude from a response.
When both are supplied, field takes precedence over exclude_field.
The quality parameter filters entities by quality.
The single-entity endpoint is /entity/{entity}.{extension}.
The single-entity endpoint requires an integer entity ID.
The single-entity endpoint supports JSON output.
The single-entity endpoint supports HTML output.
The single-entity endpoint supports GeoJSON output.
The dataset-list endpoint is /dataset.{extension}.
The dataset-list endpoint supports JSON output.
The dataset-list endpoint supports HTML output.
The include_typologies dataset-list parameter can be set false to omit typologies.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI JSON description that can be used to generate a client library.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m covers about 99% of England.
The DTM 1m has 1m spatial resolution.
DTM 1m uses the last or only laser pulse return.
DTM production removes surface objects using bespoke algorithms.
DTM production also uses manual editing to remove surface objects.
The 2022 DTM 1m combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
For repeated DTM 1m surveys the newest, best-resolution source is selected.
DTM 1m uses bilinear interpolation where source data must be resampled.
The DTM 1m composite source period begins on 6 June 2000.
The DTM 1m composite source period ends on 2 April 2022.
DTM 1m data is distributed as GeoTIFF raster data.
DTM 1m is distributed in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 1m elevations are expressed in metres.
DTM 1m elevations are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
DTM 1m uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual surveys contributing to the DTM 1m composite are documented at ±15cm vertical RMSE.
DTM 1m has no public access constraints beyond its stated licence.
DTM 1m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
DTM 1m is updated annually.
DTM 1m uses EPSG:27700.
DTM 1m metadata latitude extent is 49.943 to 55.816.
DTM 1m metadata longitude extent is -6.236 to 2.072.
DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
DTM 1m exposes WMS.
DTM 1m exposes WCS.
DTM 1m exposes WMTS.
DTM 1m exposes an OGC API Features service.
DTM 1m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
DTM 1m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The Environment Agency publishes the DTM 1m dataset.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 2m covers about 99% of England.
The DTM 2m has 2m spatial resolution.
DTM 2m uses the last or only laser pulse return.
DTM 2m source-object removal uses bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
The DTM 2m composite also combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
DTM 2m uses newest, best-resolution data where repeat surveys exist.
DTM 2m uses bilinear interpolation when resampling is required.
DTM 2m is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
DTM 2m elevations are expressed in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
DTM 2m uses OSTN15.
DTM 2m metadata identifier is 09ea3b37-df3a-4e8b-ac69-fb0842227b04.
DTM 2m exposes WMS.
DTM 2m exposes WCS.
DTM 2m exposes WMTS.
DTM 2m exposes an OGC API Features service.
DTM 2m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
DTM 2m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The LIDAR Composite DSM 1m covers about 99% of England.
DSM 1m has 1m spatial resolution.
DSM 1m uses the last or only laser pulse return.
DSM 1m retains surface objects including vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
DSM 1m combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
DSM 1m metadata identifier is 9ba4d5ac-d596-445a-9056-dae3ddec0178.
DSM 1m exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
DSM 1m exposes an OGC API Features service.
DSM 1m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
DSM 1m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
The First Return DSM 2m covers about 99% of England.
The First Return DSM 2m has 2m spatial resolution.
First Return DSM 2m uses the first or only laser return.
First Return DSM 2m includes surface objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
First Return DSM 2m derives from National LIDAR Programme capture from 11 November 2016 to 5 May 2022.
The National LIDAR Programme divided England into about 300 survey blocks for the first-return composite.
First Return DSM 2m merges surveys with feathering at overlaps.
First Return DSM coverage can differ from last-return DSM coverage because the last-return composite also uses Time Stamped surveys.
First Return DSM 2m is delivered as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
First Return DSM 2m elevations are expressed in metres relative to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
First Return DSM 2m uses OSTN15.
First Return DSM 2m metadata identifier is 54167602-36c8-4b2b-80ec-ebb6267b6b1e.
First Return DSM 2m exposes WMS, WCS and WMTS services.
First Return DSM 2m exposes an OGC API Features service.
First Return DSM 2m metadata creation date is 8 February 2023.
First Return DSM 2m metadata revision date is 15 December 2023.
DTM 10m covers about 99% of England at 10m spatial resolution.
DTM 10m is resampled from the DTM 2m composite using bilinear interpolation.
DTM 10m is supplied as a single GeoTIFF raster aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM 10m metadata identifier is ce8fe7e7-bed0-4889-8825-19b042e128d2.
DTM 10m has no web data services or area-of-interest resources listed on its dataset record.
The retired 25cm DTM composite has been replaced by the 1m composite product.
Environment Agency 25cm time-stamped archive data remains available through the survey archive.
OS Terrain 50 source terrain is captured as a triangulated irregular network (TIN).
The source TIN is edited using mass points and breaklines and can also use automated photogrammetric techniques.
Ordnance Survey describes TIN triangles as retaining feature edges more accurately than a regular grid.
Terrain 50 grid data is interpolated from the source TIN.
Terrain 50 contour data is also interpolated from the source TIN.
Terrain 50 generalises feature modelling because it is designed to work with small-scale products.
Minimum Terrain 50 coastal coverage extends to the low-water mark.
For England and Wales the low-water mark used is Mean Low Water.
For Scotland the low-water mark used is Mean Low Water Springs.
Land wholly within inland water bodies that is represented by topographic-area features is captured to the area's positional-accuracy requirements.
For such inland-water land, the minimum capture requirement is the outer edge of the feature.
Surrounding water for captured inland-water land remains flat.
Other land inside inland water bodies produced by automated processes is removed from the terrain data.
Terrain 50 source accuracy requirements classify terrain into urban/major communication routes, rural, and mountain/moorland areas.
Source TIN z values must meet positional-accuracy requirements appropriate to the geographic classification.
Terrain height accuracy is assessed against Newlyn Datum using RMSE targets.
Terrain 50 bare-earth source points use Eastings and Northings in OSGB36.
Terrain 50 source Z values are heights in metres relative to the applicable datum.
Most Terrain 50 source areas use Ordnance Survey Newlyn Datum.
A small number of offshore islands use a local vertical datum.
The bare-earth model excludes buildings.
The bare-earth model excludes supported structures.
The bare-earth model excludes vegetation.
Ground-level obstructions such as sufficiently wide dams, breakwaters and groynes can be treated as part of the bare-earth surface.
Bridge revetments and earthworks can be represented as part of the bare-earth surface.
Only terrain features expected to persist to the next revision period or longer are modelled.
Underground features are not recorded in the DTM.
Overhead features are removed from the DTM.
Terrain 50 source modelling is intended to be free of artificial spikes and wells that do not represent real terrain.
Road carriageways and railway track beds are expected to appear smooth in the terrain data.
Most Terrain 50 data should present without visible tile edges or discernible height differences between tiles.
Small tile edges can occur in tidal areas because of local tidal differences.
Supported structures such as bridges, viaducts, cranes and elevated buildings are removed where an air gap exists above bare earth.
Jetties or piers on legs are treated as supported structures and removed where they depart from bare earth.
Hedgerows and trees are removed so the bare-earth surface is represented.
For a vertical terrain feature, the top height is recorded at its correct planimetric position.
The lowest point of a vertical feature can be planimetrically offset to avoid two z values at one location.
Major communication routes are major road and rail networks identified in Ordnance Survey core data.
Road carriageway and railway track-bed limits are modelled to reflect real-world route shape.
Modelling of major routes removes extraneous features such as road furniture and bridges.
Associated slopes and embankments along major routes are modelled.
Mineral extraction and landfill outer limits, shape and depth are captured to positional-accuracy requirements.
Temporary spoil heaps that do not represent enduring terrain are removed.
Flat-water bodies larger than 0.7 hectares have their limits captured so their presence can be inferred.
For captured large flat-water bodies, water height is recorded at the lowest height of surrounding data.
Captured flat-water-body surfaces are modelled as flat.
Terrain 50 ASCII grid stores heights at pixel centres.
A 10km Terrain 50 ASCII tile contains 200 pixels per row.
Each Terrain 50 ASCII grid pixel is 50m by 50m.
Terrain 50 ASCII rows run west to east.
Successive ASCII rows begin 50m south of the previous row.
Terrain 50 ASCII heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1m.
A Terrain 50 grid delivery includes an .asc data file.
The accompanying .gml file supplies location, grid-spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata for the ASCII grid.
Terrain 50 per-tile XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
